title: Can you modify the bodyfat range in which building muscle is most comfortable?
summary: Answering a viewer, NH argues that the body fat range in which you build muscle best (e.g. 14-18%) can be moved, but only slowly and with patience, much like natural selection. Short bulk/cut cycles keep people stuck; he describes his own recomp at 17% body fat and how the window may shrink and later be widened again.
claims: Recomps confuse bulk/cut lifters, and many people who stagnate wrongly call it a recomp
Recomping at maintenance removes supposed limitations quickly; he was surprised by how his body fat distribution changed
The set point idea holds that each person has a body fat range where they are most anabolic, keep lean mass and gain the least fat
That range is not fixed; it shifts with age, accumulated training and hormonal changes
14-18% body fat is a realistic, good range for naturals to aim for; he is in it, on the higher side
There are no somatotypes; being 20% body fat now does not mean you will be forever
Some people need to be full to train well, others train better hungry because it makes them aggressive
After 48 hours of fasting your strength drops a lot
A meal eaten just before training helps mostly psychologically unless it is fast-digesting carbs, and you do not need protein right after training to build muscle
You can push the range and still stay anabolic, but the body adapts slowly, like natural selection; it is the principle of specificity applied to Darwinism
For strength, carry as much mass as possible, preferably muscle: 400 lb at 10% beats 400 lb at 20%
People feel stuck in a body fat window because their bulk/cut cycles are too short; even a six-month bulk is short
Naturals can keep progressing into their 40s, so there is no rush to gain or lose fast
Bulk slowly; gaining four pounds a month adds too much fat
A permabulk from day one for 15 years is good advice, but overshooting your body fat once ruins it
Novices run the most extreme bulk/cut cycles outside pro bodybuilding, yet they are the ones who should never do it
For six-plus months he has held his weight while lowering body fat; his legs got stronger and bigger but have lost no fat yet
The window may shrink as you move it, until you reach a true set point
When that happens, widen it again: slow bulk to gain mass and fat, then recomp again, even if the cycle takes five years
A permabulk keeps you anabolic with spare energy for building, unlike a recomp at maintenance, but some added calories inevitably become fat
